title: Auto-answer caregiver call mode
problem: The person living with dementia often cannot answer a smartphone call (swipe UI, volume, which app). Family members need a reliable way to open a loud speakerphone path from allowlisted contacts.
solution: Dedicated Android mode or cheap spare-phone image: auto-answer allowlisted contacts, force speaker, giant hangup affordance, no app clutter. Could ship as setup guide + MDM/kiosk profile, or a dedicated app.
whyWidespread: Call-answer failure is a classic middle-stage dementia friction point. Caregivers already buy simplified phones (e.g. RAZ Memory Cell Phone) and kiosk tools, so demand exists.
targetUser: Long-distance or busy caregivers who need reliable audio check-ins.
fitForGeorge: Mostly software / Android profile work. Hardware can be commodity unlocked Android phones.

feasibility.notes: Android auto-answer and call screening APIs vary by OEM/version. Accessibility + default-dialer constraints need a spike. Not a medical device if framed as convenience/kiosk.

market.willingnessToPay: Families pay hundreds for specialized senior phones. A $29-$79 app or $149 configured phone kit could work.
market.profitHypothesis: Software margin is excellent if OEM permission hurdles are solved. Hardware-kit margin is thinner but easier to explain.

softwarePlan.summary: Android app + setup profile: contact allowlist, auto-answer, max speakerphone, kiosk launcher, remote config by caregiver.
risks: False auto-answer from robocallers if allowlist fails

unsolved: Which Android OEM/API path is most reliable in 2026
